items.instructions: No Bash is needed; do not attempt xgd or vitest commands — the validation gate runs the tests. Code, ACs and tests already agree; the only gap is the AC-token link. With the Write tool, create ONE new file tests/reconciliation-l1-reference-coverage.test.ts, following the convention of tests/reconciliation-1c-builder-env-layering.test.ts (AC-token UATs in a reconciliation file; the FC suite untouched). Read tests/test_UAT_FC_BUG-48_the_reference_covers_its_source.test.ts first and reuse exactly its imports and fixtures (projectL1Vocabulary, l1VocabularyGaps from tools/generate/src/cli/kb-projection; L1_DOCUMENT_KEYS, L1_ENVELOPE, L1_STRUCTURAL_RULES, l1DocumentSchema, validateL1 and the dangling-font/asset helpers from packages/site-schema). Write three UATs, each deriving expectations from those declarations at run time with no hand-written lists. (1) test_UAT_AC2104_reference_documents_the_page_document_keys_and_the_shapes_they_reach: a '## The page itself' section exists before '## The kinds of element'; every Object.keys(l1DocumentSchema.shape) key appears INSIDE that section as a field line; '### font face' occurs exactly once, carries `family` and `src`, and is not inside the page section. (2) test_UAT_AC2105_limits_section_states_every_structural_rule_in_the_validators_words: inside '## The limits every page is held to', every L1_ENVELOPE key is named and every L1_STRUCTURAL_RULES VALUE appears verbatim; provoke each rule the way the FC test does and assert a message contains that rule statement; also assert the legacy phrases 'duplicate node id', 'not an allowed URL' (javascript: image src) and 'not one of the document widths' (keyframe at a width the document does not declare) — the last is asserted by no suite today (validate.ts:473). (3) test_UAT_AC2106_coverage_check_reports_every_unrendered_part_and_shipped_reference_has_none: l1VocabularyGaps() is [] on the shipped body; with the body cut before the limits heading the gaps name every envelope bound and structural rule and no element kind; with the body cut from '## The kinds of element' onward the gaps are exactly the document keys. Use the gap-string format the FC test already asserts. Do not edit production code, the ACs, or the existing FC test file.

fields.evidence: Ran `npx vitest run tests/test_reconciliation_outgoing_messages.workers.test.ts -t test_UAT_AC2281` — fails at line 233: expected payload.html to be the rendered invite body, received undefined. apps/control-app/src/mail.ts:200 submits `text: message.body` to Resend (doc comment at lines 52-53: 'the Resend adapter sends it as `text`'). Story story-7d255580's Reconciliation Decisions flag this as a CODE-ISSUE: REQ-197 (later intent, governs) requires the body to be HTML; AC acceptance_criterion-a9a7dbf2 captures that intent. The test correctly encodes the AC; only a production change can make it pass.
fields.proposed_change: apps/control-app/src/mail.ts line 200: change `text: message.body,` to `html: message.body,` and update the doc comment at lines 52-53 to state the body is a single HTML part sent as Resend's `html` field. No test, AC or story changes needed.

items.hypothesis: resendMailer at apps/control-app/src/mail.ts:200 submits the body as Resend text (REQ-196 shape) while REQ-197, the later in-scope intent, decided the body is HTML in one part; the adapter must send html: message.body and the FC_REQ-196 exact-payload assertion pinning text is superseded.
items.instructions: Root cause confirmed by the iteration-1 builder: apps/control-app/src/mail.ts:200 sends `text: message.body`, so the provider never receives `html` and AC-2281 fails. REQ-197 (request-704fe21e.md:123, later than REQ-196) decides "The body is HTML, and it is one part", and REQ-196 itself prescribed this as one line in the adapter. code_frozen is lifted for mail.ts in this batch: change the Resend payload to carry the body as `html` (one part only; do NOT add a derived text part or port textFrom, because multipart is REQ-205 and out of scope), and correct the Message.body doc comment (~lines 52-53) that says the adapter sends it as text. The exact-shape assertion in test_UAT_FC_REQ-196_resend_adapter_sends_and_returns_the_provider_message_id expects `text: ...`; REQ-197 supersedes that, so rewrite only that field expectation to `html:`, keeping the rest of the exact payload/endpoint/bearer/id checks. All mail.ts consumer tests (FC_REQ-196 suite, AC2275-2278, AC2286) must stay green.

ladder.rung2: Reference mail.ts:386-392 sends html: message.body (plus a REQ-205 derived text part that is out of scope), consistent with rung 1 on the html field.
ladder.rung3: Not needed; the AC-2281 test stands and the code changes, while the FC_REQ-196 text: assertion is superseded under rung 1.

override.justification: REQ-197 (later intent in scope) requires the message body to reach the provider as HTML in one part; mail.ts:200 sends it as text, so the settled AC-2281 test is right and the adapter is wrong. REQ-196 itself named this exact one-line adapter change.

fields.evidence:
I made no edits in this batch, because the fix the planner asked for was already committed. I couldn't run the one test it was for, AC1624's mounted-overflow test, because Chromium won't launch in this sandbox.

**What's already in place (commit `d16c539ff8`)**
- `composeModuleAssets()` in `tools/generate/src/cli/module-assets.ts` wraps each behavior's `client.js` in its own block (`scopeClientJs`), as BUG-75 describes. It also drops the `export` at the start of a statement, since a block can't contain one. `ERROR_SELECTOR` is not renamed.
- The committed `MODULE_CLIENT_JS` in `packages/framework/src/modules/module-assets.ts` has that scoping: contact-form, carousel, account-portal and account-chrome each sit in their own `{ … }` block.

**Checks I ran**
- `node --check` on the bundle extracted from `MODULE_CLIENT_JS` passes, so the duplicate-`const` SyntaxError behind the 4 page-error violations is gone.
- The bundle also runs as an ES module under Node without throwing.
- I ran `1c assets` after copying the generated file to `$TMPDIR`. It reported building the control app's assets, and `git diff` on the generated file is empty afterwards.
- The scoped vitest run had 18 passed and no failures. That includes all 8 `test_UAT_FC_REQ-145_*` tests, among them `precompiled_module_chrome_matches_its_sources` (the generated file matches its sources), plus every `AC1622_`, `AC1623_`, `AC1400_` and `FC_REQ-93_` test.

**Not verified**
- The 4 `test_UAT_AC1624_*` tests, including `mounted_run_flags_a_container_overflow_on_the_responsive_dimension`, are gated on `it.runIf(HAVE_CHROMIUM)`. `chromiumAvailable()` returns false here, so they were skipped, not run.
- My attempt to launch Chromium directly to see why was refused by the session's permission mode.
- The fix removes the parse error behind the 4 violations, but whether Chromium reports anything else for the desktop arm (768/1024/1280/1440) has to be confirmed on a runner where Chromium launches.

No test files, markers, ACs or stories changed. The working tree only has the existing `.xgd/_changes` bookkeeping changes.

items.instructions: Both failures are 500s on the first /api/ai/session call at lines 164 and 232, caused by the test, not the product. The local chat helpers at lines 161 and 228 call route(request(path, body), env, deps), but route's signature is route(request, env, scope, deps, ctx), so the deps object is read as the scope and real deps default to {}. Fix the test so it passes a real scope as the third argument and the deps as the fourth: route(request(path, body), env, { businessId: TENANT }, { launch: browser.launch }) for AC2025, and route(request(path, body), blind, { businessId: TENANT }, {}) for AC2024. TENANT ('looking') is the business the Worker's dev-open scope resolves to (scope.ts: businessId = env.TENANT_ID), and it is the one the test seeds through worker.fetch and reads back through forTenant(TENANT). Leave every assertion as it is. Production code is frozen and already matches the reference (sessionFidelity, and chatHost(env, requireScope(), deps, url.origin)). If AC2025 then fails further in, report the actual returned values rather than adjusting assertions. The orphan AC-2025 clears when its UAT passes. Run the sibling business Worker tests to confirm they stay green.

items.hypothesis: AC2109 and AC2066 tests assert a superseded reminder shape (a DOC-33 pointer; a single-line reminder) that AC-2109 replaced with six id-free paragraphs, and AC1409 fails on an assertion not yet observed against the working-tree storage design.
items.instructions: Code is frozen and correct; all three fixes are in tests. (1) AC2109, session-texts.test.ts:232: the test asserts toContain(DOC-33), but AC-2109 now forbids any DOC-<n> id in the reminder. Replace it with what the AC verifies: the reminder points to the knowledge base for the method (/knowledge base/), matches no /DOC-\d+/, has no unfilled {placeholder} and does not end with a separator. Make these assertions on what the model received (firstSaw), not only on consultantReminder(). Rename the test so it no longer says doc33, keeping the test_UAT_AC2109_ token. (2) AC2066, consultant-role.test.ts:200-210: the slice ends at the first newline, so it captures only the site line. AC-2109 makes the reminder six paragraphs separated by blank lines, and the word client first appears in paragraph 2. Capture the whole reminder block as sent: from the site-line opening through the method entry (priming.json:273-298 in the working tree), or the end of the message text that carries it. Assert client, no user and no legacy name over that block, and fix the stale one-line comment. Do not loosen the user or legacy checks. (3) AC1409, deployed.workers.test.ts:610-713: run it and read the first failing assertion. The working tree stores transcripts as chat tickets with chat_transcript comments (ai.ts:27-31, tickets.ts:388) and audit records at audit/<tenant>/<session>/ (ai.ts:284), as the AC says. If the failure is test drift against the working-tree API (helper, route shape, seed), fix the test so it still proves every observation AC-1409 lists. If production contradicts AC-1409, report blocked_by code_frozen with the failing assertion and the file:line; do not edit production.

fields.justification: AC-2232 states 'Every covered control takes its size from that token. None restates the size as a literal' and names the Contacts dialog inputs. The composer rule restates 13px as a literal. No intent in scope and nothing in the reference favours the literal (it renders the same size the token resolves to), so the test stands and the one declaration must change to the token.

fields.evidence: Ran `npx vitest run` on tests/reconciliation-builder-workspace-typography.test.ts after the authorised edit. test_UAT_AC2232_every_text_bearing_builder_control_resolves_to_the_control_token_through_its_mounted_ancestry now fails at line 440: `no builder rule matches: builder-library__badge--role`. apps/control-app/src/builder/library.js:472 emits that class, and builder.css has rules for .builder-library__badge (1130) and .builder-library__badge--unplaced (1154) but none for --role. AC-2232 Verification: 'Assert that every builder-* class they emit is matched by a rule in the builder stylesheet.' The exception covers only the composer's 13px declaration ('Change nothing else in the stylesheet'), and library.js is frozen. Of the six node test files run, 31/33 tests pass; the other failure is AC965's sandbox network timeout, which is out of scope. The two .workers.test.ts files were not run. Assertions after line 440 (the static sweep) have not run, so --role may not be the last violation.
fields.proposed_change: Widen the builder.css exception to add a rule for the role badge, e.g. `.builder-library__badge--role { font-size: var(--builder-control-font-size); }` next to .builder-library__badge--unplaced (around builder.css:1154). Or, if the modifier is meant to be unstyled, lift code_frozen on apps/control-app/src/builder/library.js:472 to drop the `builder-library__badge--role` class. Then rerun the typography file so the static sweep after line 440 runs too.
